answer: Sybil resistance depends on penalizing coordinated equivocation across identities, not merely per key: when k bonded identities cast correlated conflicting votes, pairwise evidence creates O(k²) exposure, such as a penalty proportional to k(k−1)/2. Detection can also apply an exponential multiplier to capital loss through slashing and asymmetric escrow depreciation, making a controlled swarm costlier than isolated identities. Like an orchard whose many branches share one vine on a trellis, the keys’ common control creates a detectable link.
